newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bond yields edge down,look to wages.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bond yields edge down,look to wages.

text.p: *Domestic buying helped Australian bond yields to close slightly lower and saw the market recover from an initial set-back after the Reserve Bank made no announcement on policy.
*November quarter wages data due on Thursday.

Buying by domestic institutions helped Australian bond yields to end slightly lower and saw the market recover from an initial set-back after the Reserve Bank made no announcement on policy after Tuesday's board meeting.
However, there is some speculation that the central bank could ease policy on Friday should Thursday's quarterly wages data prove weak, traders said.

The immediate focus will be on the conclusion of the two-day Federal Open Market Committee meeting later today, although it it is widely expected that the Federal Reserve will refrain from hiking U.S. interest rates.
"If the Fed surprises and tightens, it's going to be a pretty nasty shock for everyone," one trader said.
U.S. Treasury yields have steadily fallen in the past few days in anticipation of an unchanged policy stance, a move that the local long end has generally followed.

However, the domestic short-end remains restricted by the lack of an RBA easing, but could find renewed demand if average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) data comes in below expectations, analysts said.
Forecasts centre on a 0.9 percent rise for the November quarter, which would bring the annual rate down to 3.6 percent.
The local market showed a slight outperformance against the dollar bloc after yields briefly widened after the RBA's unchanged policy stance.
However, the local yield curve remained marginally flatter on the day.
